newsitem.title: GERMANY: Documenta sponsors see art as offbeat showcase.
newsitem.headline: Documenta sponsors see art as offbeat showcase.

text.p: Corporate sponsors of documenta X, Germany's leading international art exhibition, say they are using art to show off their technology and products, and reach their customers in a different way.

German railway Deutsche Bahn has splashed the exhibition's "dx" logo on the locomotives of all its high-speed ICE express trains, and is showing video reports on documenta in waiting areas of stations around the country.
It has provided Kassel's old main rail station as one of documenta's prime exhibition spaces, and is offering special fares to visit the show from around the country.
Documenta X, billed as "the world's leading exhibition of contemporary art", will open on Saturday and continue until September 28.

Sony Corp has been a documenta sponsor since 1977. This year it supplied film and video equipment for many artists and will be providing Internet transmission of the "100 Guests" lecture series -- one lecture for each day of the show.
"With our engagement in Kassel, we will be using art as a platform for us as a leading multimedia company," Caroline Ruppert, sponsoring manager of Sony Deutschland, said in a statement.
The Sparkassen Group of community banks, another documenta sponsor, spent 34 million marks ($19.6 million) on supporting the arts in 1996.
"We are convinced that art and culture are indispensible raw material for an open society, a form of nourishment," said Horst Koehler, president of the German Sparkassen and Giroverband.
IBM Deutschland GmbH is providing Internet support, while Volkswagen AG helped construct the work "Executive Box" by British artist Adam Page.
Other corporate sponsors include Binding Brauerei, SBK Software und Systeme Kassel GmbH and Deutsche Staedtereklame GmbH. ($ = 1.731 German Marks)
